tekno_tuning_notes.fdiff: Thinner front diff can increase off-power steering but may be twitchy; thicker increases on-power steering and stability (NTM p31).
tekno_tuning_notes.cdiff: Thicker center: less off-power steering and on-power rear traction, more on-power steering and acceleration if traction is available; thinner: the opposite (NTM p31).
tekno_tuning_notes.rdiff: Thinner rear: more off-power steering, less traction into a corner, less on-power steering, more traction out of a corner; thicker the opposite; too thin/thick = inconsistent (NTM p31).
tekno_tuning_notes.sway: Thicker bar = less roll = less grip. Front bar mainly affects off-power entry steering; rear bar mainly on-power steering and stability mid-corner/exit (NTM p32).
tekno_tuning_notes.spring: Softer = more traction through turns, more roll, slower response, better in bumps; stiffer = more corner speed if traction is available, jumps/lands better (NTM p32).
tekno_tuning_notes.piston: Smaller holes for smoother tracks with big jumps (usually thinner oil); larger holes for rougher tracks with fewer jumps (NTM p32).
tekno_tuning_notes.oil: Kit oil is a good start ~75°F; change viscosity with ~5°C / 10°F temperature change (NTM p17, p32).
tekno_tuning_notes.toe: Always some toe-out; more toe-out = more off-power steering, less on-power steering (NTM p30).
tekno_tuning_notes.camber: More negative camber quickens rotation; less negative is easier to drive (NTM p30).
tekno_tuning_notes.ride: Set ride height ready-to-run (fuel/battery in, body on); measure flat part of chassis (NTM p30).
tekno_tuning_notes.rc: Rear hub: lower axle height (higher pin position) = more roll and rear traction; higher axle = less roll, quicker direction change. Front axle: lower = more steering (TKR9141/9141B, NTM p31).
tekno_tuning_notes.wheelbase: Shorter rear wheelbase = more steering into turns/off-power; longer = better on open/bumpy tracks (NTM p31).

discrepancies: NT48 2.2 Box Stock sheet (NTM p34) prints A/B block parts as TKR9161/9161B and TKR9162/9162B; parts list (NTM p29) and assembly step (NTM p11) show TKR9461B / TKR9462B.
NTM p30 setup text suggests 23mm/25mm ride height and +4/-4mm droop (buggy-style values); the NT48 2.2 sheet and build steps use 34mm/38mm and 0/-8mm, which match ETM p27.
Diff oil: Box Stock sheet and build steps 10k/10k/5k vs setup notes "we recommend 7k front / 5k center / 5k rear" (both manuals).
ET48 2.2 springs: Box Stock sheet and build steps L-4/M-4 show TKR6090; ET parts list (ETM p26) and teknorc.com list TKR6091 (green, 5.17 lb/in) as included with the ET48 2.2 kit.

ET48 2.2 rear upper shock: ETM p18 text says “second from the inside on the tower” and the ET Box Stock sheet (ETM p30) marks exactly that hole (hole 3 of 4); NTM p18 / NT sheet: second from the outside (hole 2).
NT clutch springs: sheet "2× Red, 2× Gold" vs NTM p23 "kit contains 2× 1.0mm yellow and 2× 1.1mm red springs".
NTM p31 rear axle text names TKR9287/TKR9087 (not in the NT48 2.2 parts list); ETM p28 names TKR9687/TKR9487, which match the kit parts.
Front toe: sheet 2° out vs setup notes "approximately 0.5–1 degree of toe out per side".
NB48 2.2 ride height: Box Stock sheet (NBM p35) and build steps (NBM p17/p18) say 24mm front / 26mm rear; the setup notes (NBM p30) say 23mm / 25mm. EB48 2.2 uses 23 / 25 everywhere.
NB48 2.2 clutch springs: sheet “2x Green, 2x Gold” vs NBM p23 “(2x) 0.9mm green springs, (2x) 1.0mm yellow springs”.
EB48 2.2 parts list page (EBM p26) is headed “TKR9003 – EB48 2.1 … Kit”; the kit body is listed as TKR9045 (EB48 2.0) and the NB48 body as TKR9345B (NB48 2.1) – carry-over parts, not 2.2-specific.
teknorc.com titles TKR6032B “rear” spring, but both buggy kits use TKR6032B front AND rear (sheet + build steps).
Buggy setup notes (NBM p30 / EBM p27) suggest a good starting point of the “F” plate and TKR9047F spindle arm – the Box Stock sheet also marks F, consistent.

NB48 2.2: the newer v3 sheet (rev 260520) has no front UNI/CVD choice, no CVD rear option, no +4mm standoff and no TKR9416 0mm bulkhead – old setups that use them keep the value as “custom” (with an import/migration warning).
gaps: Tires/inserts/wheels: not specified for either kit (sheet blank).
Engine, pipe, fuel, plug (NT) and ESC, motor, battery (ET): not included / not specified.
No nitro gearing chart or optional clutch bell / spur sizes for NT48 2.2 in the manual (only 13t/48t stock).
Front shock standoff +4mm part number not listed.
Achievable kick-up / anti-squat / toe / sweep values for non-center insert positions are not tabulated (only center-dot values: kick-up 10°, sweep 0°, anti-squat 3°, rear toe 2.5°).
Roll-center numbers (mm) are not published; only directional notes.
Rear hub (15-hole) and tower hole numbering beyond the "2/5" and "3/B" stock notes is inferred from the drawings.
Shock oil and diff oil dropdown lists are generic viscosities (Tekno does not publish an option list).
NB48/EB48: no overall dimensions or weight published (teknorc.com lists them as not specified), so the buggy artwork proportions are illustrative only.
NB48/EB48: which hole size of the mixed TKR6138 / TKR6139 piston sets is used front vs rear is not stated.
NB48/EB48: no camber-link turnbuckle lengths printed; no published spring rate/colour for TKR6035/6036/6037/6039.
NB48 2.2: no nitro gearing chart (only 13t bell / 48t spur stock, 46t/47t optional spurs listed).
Tires, wheels, inserts, engine/pipe, ESC/motor/battery: not included in the buggy kits / left blank on the sheets.

mip.assembly: Piston, then valve, then stop washer, secured with the locknut. Start with the Blue (medium) valve. Keep the oil, piston-hole setup, springs and ride height you ran before (MIPI p1).

tuning_notes.t: Valves tune REBOUND (return) speed without changing shock oil weight; on impact the valve shims open to let oil bypass the primary holes (MIP: reduces shock packing in rapid bumps).
Valve chart: FAST (rough) = thin Green .003", MEDIUM = Blue .005", SLOW (smooth) = Clear/Matte .007".
If Medium rebounds too fast but Slow is too slow, stack valves (e.g. Tan .004" under Green .003") to fine-tune.
Hi-Flow pistons have a smaller outer diameter: more blow-by at slow shaft speeds; MIP claims better jumping, landing and bump recovery. They can be mixed front/rear with standard Bypass1.
High-grip, rutted tracks: high-flow setup with faster rebound valves so the suspension drops into ruts and keeps cornering traction.
High-speed chop & big jumps: firmer valve stacks to prevent bottoming over big jumps while soaking up small chatter.

mip.oil: MIP publishes no oil range for Bypass1: the instructions say to keep the oil you ran before (MIPI p1).
gaps: #19010 Tekno-specific set is not listed on miponline.com right now; fitment of #19021/#19011 to Tekno is not stated on their pages (inferred from the #19010 set they replace).
MIP publishes no bleed/bypass hole diameters for the valve-covered ports, no recommended oil range, and no shock-dyno numbers.
Tapered Hi-Flow #24400 page says both “6-Hole x 1.3mm” and “4 precision-drilled 1.3mm holes”.

MIP does not publish the internal port/flow layout or how valve thickness affects compression; the app's flow diagram is a simplified illustration of MIP's wording (valve opens on impact; thickness sets rebound speed).
Dealer listings quote MIP saying Bypass1 is dyno-tuned to match stock-piston compression and that Tekno pistons can be drilled out; not found on miponline.com, so not used.
No MIP guidance for Tekno-specific front vs rear valve choices.
